key_insight: A modular LLM pipeline can generate longitudinal synthetic clinical notes that stay internally consistent across a patient’s hospital journey while preserving stylistic diversity.
clinical_relevance: The dataset offers privacy-preserving text for building and testing clinical AI tools such as summarizers, coding models, and decision support systems without using real patient notes.
method: Structured patient profiles are generated first.
A semi-structured patient journey is simulated across time.
LLMs then create unstructured clinical notes, with validation and augmentation steps to improve realism and faithfulness.
evidence_signal: The release includes 70 synthetic patients with 20–50 notes each, provided at multiple validation levels to balance realism and scalability.
watch_item: Synthetic notes may still miss rare clinical nuances or hidden inconsistencies, so suitability depends on the intended downstream use and validation level.
paper_title: A Pipeline for Generating Longitudinal Synthetic Clinical Notes Using Large Language Models
